subject: maths
question: The marked price of an item is ₹27,500. The shopkeeper gave two successive discounts: the first discount was 20%, and the second was 30% of the first discount rate. What is the selling price of the item (in rupees)?
solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹27,500

First discount = 20%

Second discount = 30% of first discount rate

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

**Calculations:**

Second discount rate = 30% of 20%

⇒ Second discount = 30/100 × 20 = 6%

⇒ SP = 27,500 × (1 − 20/100) × (1 − 6/100)

⇒ SP = 27,500 × 80/100 × 94/100

⇒ SP = 27,500 × 0.8 × 0.94

⇒ SP = 27,500 × 0.752

⇒ SP = 20,680

**∴ The selling price of the item is ₹20,680.**
